clue.text: Biological set-up could be destroyed by comets, yes?

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so the letters of these two words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A doomsday question: could a swarm of comets wipe out life's arrangements?
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be destroyed' rearranges COMETS plus YES; the comma and question mark are only dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecosystem is a community of living things and their environment, a natural biological arrangement.

clue.text: Headgear made of gold, one seen in court

indicators.note: the gold and the one are placed inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golden crown is spotted on someone at a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the container signal: the gold and the one sit inside the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn on the head, a type of headgear.

clue.text: American underground worker sadly has no dig when one has been cancelled

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words are in a sorry, jumbled state, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A miner laments that he has nothing to dig once a job has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' jumbles HAS NO DIG, and 'when one has been cancelled' takes out I (one), leaving seven letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandhog is US slang for a labourer who digs tunnels or caissons beneath ground or water.

clue.text: Team, one from Madrid involving stars

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
Real Madrid is the famous football club, so Real is one from Madrid

explanation.surface: Football talk: a team, and one of them from Madrid, featuring star players.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at star footballers, but 'involving stars' is the definition, of the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal means relating to or measured by the stars, as in a sidereal day.

clue.text: The old man upset about labour's leader being seen as jester-like

indicators.note: the reversed old word and man are placed around the next letter
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: ye is the old form of the
a tom is a male animal, so man

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A father is angry about the head of the Labour Party looking like a clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes MOTEY, and 'about' wraps that around the leader of 'labour's'; 'The old' is archaic language, not a father.
explanation.definitionFit: Motley was the multicoloured costume of a court fool, so as an adjective it describes a jester's look.

clue.text: Resist lie, coming out clean

indicators.note: coming out suggests the letters emerge in a different order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to refuse falsehood and emerge with a clear conscience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' rearranges RESIST and LIE together; 'clean' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To sterilise something is to make it free of germs, a thorough kind of cleaning.

clue.text: Rod has desire to eat pepper

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the rod swallows the word for desire

parts.note: a cane is a rod or stick
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Someone called Rod fancies something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name but is a stick; 'to eat' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper made from dried chillies.

clue.text: Factional group, about a hundred, following early heretic

indicators.note: the heretic comes after the first part
the word for group goes about, that is around, the letter for a hundred

parts.note: a set is a group of things
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
an Arian followed Arius, a fourth-century churchman condemned as a heretic

explanation.surface: Some hundred dissenters form a breakaway group following an ancient heresy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Factional group' reads as one phrase, but only 'Factional' defines; 'about' is the container and 'following' the order signal. Arius was condemned at Nicaea in 325.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectarian describes people divided into rival parties or sects, so partisan and factional.

clue.text: It's shocking, silver being pocketed — great indignation!

indicators.note: a pocketed thing is put inside something, so silver goes inside the word for shocking

parts.note: outré means shockingly unconventional
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A theft of silver provokes a furious shout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's shocking' looks like an exclamation but supplies the French loanword outré; 'being pocketed' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is a feeling of intense anger and indignation at something offensive.

clue.text: Soldier may have chucked it in

definitions.text: Soldier may have chucked it in

parts.words: Soldier may have chucked it in
parts.note: chucked it in sounds like giving up a job, but read literally it is a small bomb that a soldier throws into a trench or room

explanation.surface: A soldier has perhaps quit the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucked it in' is idiom for resigning; the cryptic reading is a soldier lobbing a weapon in.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small explosive device thrown by hand, which soldiers toss into enemy positions.

clue.text: Learner heading east from French port

indicators.note: the learner letter heads, that is comes in front of, the other piece

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate letter
the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: A novice travels east from a harbour in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorient is a naval and fishing harbour town in Brittany, on France's Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Port in a cell used by hermit

definitions.meaning: a place where ships may moor, also the name of a city in Alaska
a religious recluse, an anchorite, lived walled up in a small cell bearing this name

explanation.surface: A harbour inside a hermit's cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is archaic: an anchorite's dwelling was so called.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour where vessels lie at anchor, and also the enclosed cell of a medieval religious recluse.

clue.text: European wanting English to be relevant

parts.note: a German is a European

explanation.surface: A continental who lacks English hopes to stay pertinent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like 'lacking', which would remove a letter, but here it means 'needing', so E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means pertinent or closely connected to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Look at ship's cosmetic addition

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Inspecting a vessel's makeup.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is make-up drawn along the lash line to accentuate the eyes.

clue.text: In the morning soldier gets knocked over on the street? Shame!

indicators.note: the reversed pieces sit on, that is follow, the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is mugged in the street one morning: how disgraceful!
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' makes IGMA from the morning and soldier pieces; 'on' sets it after the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace or dishonour attached to someone.

clue.text: Running aground in position across river

indicators.note: the word for position stretches across, that is around, the river letter

parts.note: standing is one's position or status

explanation.surface: A boat runs aground in a position spanning a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranding is a ship being driven onto a shore or bank and stuck there.

clue.text: What's put into fireworks could be amusing me

indicators.note: could be signals that the words may become something else when the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds a firework display entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges AMUSING ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium is a metal that burns with a brilliant white light, so it is used in flares and sparklers.

clue.text: Old student gangster, university male the reverse of a star

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

indicators.note: the reverse of the word for a star means it is read backwards

parts.note: the Sun is a star

explanation.surface: A former student turned mobster, a university man, is the opposite of a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the reverse of' turns SUN into NUS at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a graduate or former pupil of a school or university.

clue.text: Not fit for employment and impotent outside America

indicators.note: the word for impotent sits outside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: unable means powerless or incapable
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A worker is declared unemployable and powerless abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal; 'impotent' here means powerless rather than anything sexual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusable cannot be put to use, so is unsuitable for any service.

clue.text: You may hold dad to be a very important person

indicators.note: the old word for you holds, that is contains, the word for dad

parts.note: thee is the old form of you
pop is an informal name for dad

explanation.surface: You might regard your father as a VIP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold dad' suggests esteem for a father; 'may hold' is the container signal around the archaic 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of the Roman Catholic Church is a supremely important figure, which makes him a VIP.

clue.text: Sailor in the hold

definitions.meaning: Horatio, Admiral Lord, the British naval hero of Trafalgar
a wrestling grip in which the arms are locked behind the opponent's neck

explanation.surface: A seaman down in the ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' suggests a ship's cargo space; it is a wrestling grip, the full or half nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral Horatio was a famous seaman, and the wrestler's half or full nelson is a grip.

clue.text: Feature of trees in meadow beginning to fade and get old

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to age is to get old

explanation.surface: In a meadow, the trees begin to fade and grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is foliage, the leaves that clothe trees.

clue.text: Abuse of cocaine, mainly

definitions.note: an adverb definition: of the main, the sea

indicators.note: abuse suggests misuse and mistreatment, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Drug misuse, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' looks like 'for the most part' but means 'of the main', the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the open sea, so something oceanic belongs to it.

clue.text: Greek ace subsequently meeting Scot?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
then means afterwards or subsequently
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Greek champion later encounters a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the city of Athens is a Greek.

clue.text: Response coming from Americans we regretted

indicators.note: the letters come out of the run of words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: A reply from some Americans voicing regret.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside americANS WE Regretted.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a reply or response to a question.

clue.text: Fresh healthy town for each standard, say

parts.note: new means fresh
a spa is a resort town with healthy mineral waters
per means for each

explanation.surface: A new health resort sets the bar for each visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a norm but is the London Evening Standard, an example, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Evening Standard is a London daily paper, an example of the press.

clue.text: Chucks out quantities of medicine, old record having been kept

indicators.note: something kept is held within, so the record goes inside the medicine word

parts.note: doses are measured amounts of medicine
an EP is an extended-play record, an old format

explanation.surface: Someone throws away their medicine, but keeps an old vinyl disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chucks out' could be the anagram cue but is the definition; 'having been kept' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose is to remove a ruler from office, throwing them out of power.

clue.text: Gets old boy to lead army in south

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former pupil gets to command troops in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or get hold of it.

clue.text: Write about air that circulates in space

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for write is read backwards

parts.note: to pen is to write
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: Compose a song about a melody that spreads through the void.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes NEP; 'circulates' looks like a reversal cue but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is a planet that orbits the Sun in outer space.

clue.text: Respect when there's new leader? It may help if one wants a job

definitions.text: It may help if one wants a job

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: deference is polite respect

explanation.surface: Respect is due when a new boss arrives; it might help you land the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when there's new leader' changes the first letter of DEFERENCE, D, for R; the new letter is not clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference is a testimonial from a former employer, which supports an application for work.
